name: TextEditor
summary: A bounded rich-text editor with a portable Mux document value.

obligations: Expose the accessible name, descriptions, required, disabled, read-only, and invalid state on the editable content.
Expose toolbar button names and pressed state.
Keep the editable region keyboard operable.
Expose the color popup as a dialog with a labelled custom color field.
Expose the selection actions bar as a named toolbar whose controls, field, and expanded state have names, and announce pending, review, and failure states in a polite live region.
Keep focus in the editor when the selection actions bar appears, and let the keyboard enter and leave the bar without losing the selection.

behavior: A finite document value is controlled or internally managed.

A document contains blocks only: paragraphs and headings contain inline text and hard breaks; lists contain nonempty list-item sequences beginning with a paragraph; block quotes contain nonempty block sequences; code blocks contain plain text; horizontal rules and images are atomic blocks.
Safe marks preserve bold, italic, underline, strike, code, links, colors, font families, and font sizes.
The simple toolbar renders Bold, Italic, Underline, Color, alignment, and Bullet list controls with separators; advanced adds font selects, Link, Image, and Generate with AI.
Color opens a 16-swatch popup with a custom hex ColorField.
Image requests a durable http(s) image URL when no onImageRequest callback is supplied; consumers can own file uploads and insert their durable URL through that callback.
Toolbar requests use finite actions and can be controlled with onGenerate.
When bubbleMenu is enabled, a selection-driven Bold, Italic, Underline, and Link toolbar appears only for a nonempty selection and dismisses when the selection collapses.
The bubble menu is separate from the floating toolbar position.

Providing onSelectionRequest enables selection actions: a bar anchored under a nonempty selection, flipping above and staying inside the viewport, while the editor is editable and focused or the bar has focus. It never takes focus, hides when the editor is disabled or read-only, and keeps the selected range painted while focus is in the bar.

The bar holds a Describe edits field that sends on Enter (never during IME composition), the caller-supplied selectionActions with their icons, and a More actions control that expands overflow actions inline. Typing replaces the actions with a Send control. selectionInstruction false removes the field.

An action or instruction calls onSelectionRequest with the request and a controller holding a snapshot of the selected text and document, an AbortSignal, replace, insertAfter, and close. A returned promise shows the pending text (pendingLabel or Editing…) with a Cancel control; a rejection shows a fixed failure message with Try again and Dismiss.

replace and insertAfter apply once, and return false when the request is stale, aborted, over limit, invalid, or the editor is disabled or read-only. A string is plain text taking the formatting at the start of the selection, for insertAfter too; a document keeps its own formatting. An edit or formatting change of the selected range, a controlled value change, Escape, Cancel, a new request, close, or unmount aborts the signal, and close also hides the bar until the selection changes while keeping any applied edit.

After an edit applies, the new content stays highlighted with Keep, Discard, and Try again. Keep ends the review, Discard undoes the edit exactly and reselects the original range, and Try again discards and resends the same request. The edit is one undo step, and Discard leaves no extra step.

Alt+F10 from the editor moves focus into the bar, arrow keys, Home, and End move between its controls, and Escape or Tab return focus to the editor with the selection intact. Escape in the editor hides the bar until the selection changes, or cancels a pending request.
accessibility: The editable content carries its name and form-like states.
Formatting actions expose named toggle buttons.
The color dialog and custom ColorField expose their names to assistive technology.
The selection formatting toolbar exposes named controls.

The selection actions toolbar exposes named actions, a named Describe edits field, an expanded state on More actions, and a busy state while a request runs, and a polite live region announces pending, review, and failure states.

requirements.reason: Native colors do not apply to web React.
Native font metrics do not apply to web React.
